name: Soulbound Sect
reason: The source faction 'Spirit Martial Holy Land' (also rendered 'Lingwu Holy Land' / 'Spiritual Martial Holy Land' in the translation) was renamed 'Soulbound Sect' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: One of the three great tenth-rank Holy Lands of the human race in the Upper Realm, which Zane joins after his ascension. It is a vast, normally peaceful territory organized under city lords and Hall Masters; crossing it alone is a long journey. Freya's uncle serves as a city lord within it, and it produced Fenton, the greatest genius of its younger generation.

name: Sacred Feather Sea
reason: The source term 'Heavenly Feather Sacred Sea' (also rendered 'Heavenly Feather Sacred Ocean') was shortened and localized as 'Sacred Feather Sea' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A mysterious sea of miracles at the center of the Divine Kingdoms' continent and the source of the Union's power; the kingdoms' important cities and fortresses are built around it. It contains four Secret Territories, and warriors earn status by bringing resources back from it, though one careless look at it is said to be able to kill. Zane later passes the Halls of Causality trials to reach it.

name: Thundergust
reason: The unwieldy literal source name 'Thunder Wind Ghost Divine Sword' (also rendered 'Thundergale Ghost Sword' / 'Thunder Wind Divine Sword') was condensed into the punchier single-word weapon name 'Thundergust'.
description: Zane's sword in the Upper Realm arc (Eps 1048+), a Grade-One Divine Weapon of unknown origin that channels both lightning and wind blades. He wields it in the Illusionary Arena and against enemies like Julius, and the mere sight of it drawn is enough to make a Saint Lord go still.

name: Eden
issues: Gender signal check: the NovelHi translation renders Cui Yun with inconsistent pronouns (mixed he/she in the same scenes, signal m12/f16), while the episodes consistently treat Eden as male ('Maddox's son', m32/f1). The adaptation's male reading matches the character's role as Maddox's (Cui Xie's) son.
reason: The character's Chinese name Cui Yun was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Eden' was chosen for Maddox's prized heir, and the surname 'Caldwell' sets his branded identity as 'the son of the greatest fighter in The Heartlands' while keeping him nominally independent of the Maddox name.
description: Maddox's son and a rival to Zane, introduced at the Martial Tournament (Eps 491+) as an independent fighter with Divine-level talent. An Inner-Core Realm cultivator who has comprehended the Wind and Metal Laws, he wields the Relic-Class Nameless Saber and behaves with the shameless arrogance his father's backing affords him. His spirit is ultimately broken by Zane.

name: Little Monster
reason: The source epithet 'Little Monster' was carried over unchanged, as the English nickname already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: A strange, long-necked monster-like fighter from the Divine Kingdoms arc (Eps 812-874), sent to fight on Bai Yuerong's counterpart's behalf in the source. The upper echelons of the four divine kingdoms keep the true source of his gift a tight secret, and he is regarded as a different kind of danger altogether. He grins through fights and boasts of beating Zane with raw physical strength rather than Vitality.

name: Perrin Lowell
reason: The character's Chinese name Luo Peiran was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Perrin' was chosen as a sound-adjacent echo of 'Peiran', and the family surname 'Lowell' keeps him inside Zane's family unit as his cousin.
description: Zane's cousin and an early family antagonist (Eps 1-30, with later references to Ep 329). The favored young master of the Lowell family, he stole Zane's Aether Crystal, gloated over Zane's enslavement, and was accepted into the Skyreach Sect ahead of him. His standing collapses as Zane rises, and he ultimately fails to maintain his place in the Sect.

name: Marilyn
reason: The character's Chinese name Si Miaoling was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Marilyn', a feminine name fitting her polished, dangerous presence as Maddox's protegee.
description: A powerful female antagonist taken under Maddox's wing (official disciple status unclear), first seen as an escort sent by Maddox in Ep 351. She possesses the Violet-Core Physique (source: Extreme Violet Yin Body) and mid-stage Inner-Core Realm cultivation, making her a key component of Maddox's Soul Harvesting Ritual and Zane's sworn kill target. She dominates the Martial Tournament and duels Zane for the Dragon Soar Arena before being brought down (Eps 508-514, matching Si Miaoling's arc in chapters 495-502).

name: Marilyn Maddox
issues: Extraction artifact, not a real name: the episodes contain 'Marilyn, Maddox' as a comma-separated list (Eps 508, 514, 520), never 'Marilyn Maddox' as a surname-bearing name. Marilyn and Maddox are two separate characters.

name: Shane
issues: Merged entity: 'Shane' names two different characters. Captain Shane of the Imperial Army leads the Razorwing campaign (Eps 63-79, source: Lu Xiao, who 'led everyone to a building' in ch 49 exactly as Shane does in Ep 64). A second, unrelated Shane appears in Eps 631-663 as a Tower of Sin seat controller ranked eighteenth, working under Maurice and Malcolm. These should be tracked as separate characters.
reason: The character's Chinese name Lu Xiao was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Shane', a plain soldierly name fitting an Imperial Army captain.
description: Captain Shane is a military leader in the Imperial Army's Razorwing (saber insect) campaign (Eps 63-79) who hosts Zane's group of sect disciples at the Dragon Castle outpost. His hospitality is genuine but also strategic, and he is initially skeptical that Zane belongs among the veterans. Note that the unrelated Tower of Sin seat holder also called Shane (Eps 631-663) is a different character.

name: Corrupted Divine Kingdom
reason: The source faction 'Kingdom of Evil Deities' (Cui Xie's power) was renamed 'Corrupted Divine Kingdom' to read naturally alongside the adaptation's existing 'Divine Kingdom' terminology.
description: The dark power founded by Maddox in The Heartlands (Eps 688-957), which expands at frightening speed by swallowing the region's sects and grows into the largest force in the land. Its lord is Maddox himself, and no one dares call it 'just another faction' to his face. It sends spies and armies after targets like Cora, cutting off reinforcements from Cloud Hall and the World Merchants' Guild.

name: Owen
issues: Name collision / merged entity: 'Owen' refers to two different characters. Owen Lowell, Zane's uncle, appears in Eps 13-89 (see separate entry). A completely different Owen, a wealthy saint-level genius from The Fleecy Downs, competes in the Martial Tournament pre-qualifiers (Eps 452-509), is defeated by Marilyn, and reappears as Zane's ally in Eps 734-765 and 933. Their mentions must not be folded into one entity.
reason: 'Owen' is kept as the standalone name of the independent fighter from The Fleecy Downs; no confident source-novel counterpart was identified among the presented candidates.
description: An independent, wealthy fighter and saint-level genius from The Fleecy Downs, at the Ultimate level of the Soul Realm, who found a treasure hoard there. He competed in the Martial Tournament pre-qualifiers alongside Zane, driven by the same goal of killing Marilyn and stopping Maddox's Soul Harvesting Ritual, but Marilyn defeated him and nearly destroyed him. He later reunites with Zane as a friendly face (Eps 734-765, 933). Distinct from Owen Lowell, Zane's uncle.

name: Owen Lowell
reason: The character's Chinese name Luo Junyi was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Owen' was chosen for the outwardly respectable uncle, with the family surname 'Lowell' binding him into Zane's family unit.
description: Zane's uncle and an early family antagonist (Eps 13-30, 89). Behind his respectable gentleman's mask, he used deceit and poison to murder his own brother, Zane's father, and he presides over family affairs, announcing Perrin's sect acceptance. Zane beats him in a fight for his freedom (Ep 17); in the source he is later exposed as the second mastermind of the family's betrayal.

name: Streamer
reason: The literal source name 'Flowing Light Sword' was condensed into the evocative single-word name 'Streamer', per the show's established weapon-naming style (canonically NOT 'Streamer Sword').
description: Zane's signature sword through the middle arcs (Eps 218-1009), a Mythic Weapon forged by Chase and named by Zane himself. It is so sharp that a cut leaves no blood on the blade, and it serves as the channel for Zane's sword radiance and Malice-infused techniques.

name: Emanuel Drew
issues: MasterLS note is outdated: it lists Emanuel Drew as 'referenced (off-screen)' at Ep 385, but he appears on-screen from Ep 404 onward and plays an active role through the Eps 519-533 arc.
reason: The character known in the source only as 'Mister Zhuo' (Zhuo Bufan's powerful father) was given the full US-origin name 'Emanuel Drew', creating a family unit with his son Frank (source Zhuo Bufan).
description: Frank's father and one of the most powerful figures in the Cloud Hall sphere, easily on par with top elders like Saint Morphens and second only to Elder Imogen and Tia. A man in his prime at the absolute zenith of his power, he is slick, wealthy, and willing to pay insane prices for what he wants; stewards like Sir Kenneth are powerless to intervene when he is present. He leads an entourage into the palace to confront Tia after the tournament debacle (Eps 519-524).

name: Emanuel and Saint Morphens
reason: Conjunction fragment joining two existing characters (Emanuel Drew and Saint Morphens), not an entity.

name: Dragon Soar Arena
reason: The source term 'Rising Dragon Arena' was localized as 'Dragon Soar Arena', a near-synonymous rename that keeps the dragon imagery while reading more naturally in English.
description: An ancient arena-artifact and the grand prize of the Martial Tournament (Eps 430-1001), priceless to any sect or family because it accumulates Light of Fortune and connects to the Upper World. It was relocated to Oracle City, and only Zane can activate its teleportation array. Marilyn's sworn goal to claim it drives her duel with Zane.

name: Maurice
reason: The character's Chinese name Meng Chong was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Maurice', a weighty name fitting the Tower's most senior enforcer.
description: The second seat out of all one hundred and twenty-eight seat holders and the strongest fighter in the Tower of Sin (Eps 609-680). He wears fiery red armor traced with lava-like glowing lines, radiates volcanic heat, and outranks even peak War Lords like Elder May and Madeline of the Demon Night. He leads the ten seat holders against Zane, fights him on the tenth floor, and ends up utterly defeated, later directing seat controllers like Shane and Timothy to ambush Zane at the Dark Nether Cave.

name: Crystal Cube
issues: Early name drift: Ep 27 alone calls the currency 'Power Crystals' before the canonical 'Crystal Cubes' settles in; they are the same currency (and are distinct from Aether Crystals).
reason: The source currency 'Square Crystals' was localized as 'Crystal Cubes', preserving the cube/square shape idea in a cleaner English coinage.
description: The standard currency of the early and middle arcs (Eps 27-1004), used for everything from auction bids and weapon purchases to bank notes issued by tellers. Prices range from a thirty-Cube Lightning Horse to auction bids in the tens of thousands, and merchants like Corbin keep literal mountains of them.

name: Divine Kingdom
reason: The source term 'Divine Kingdom' (also rendered 'Divine Nation') was carried over directly, as it already fits the adaptation's register.
description: The great kingdoms across the Chaotic Astral Ocean from the Heartlands, remnants of the Union of Seven Divine Kingdoms that fought the Dragon-blooded; three were destroyed by the True Dragon's breath and four survive. Their cities are built around the Sacred Feather Sea, and their envoys and geniuses appear as formidable outsiders in the Heartlands arcs (Eps 532-1107) before Zane travels to the kingdoms themselves.

name: Malice
reason: The source concept 'murderous aura' / 'killing intent' was renamed 'Malice' as a single capitalized game-like stat term; Ep 302 defines it explicitly as 'just another name for a killing aura'.
description: A dark energy that clings to those who have killed, from soldiers to bandits, and can never be washed away (Eps 302-1159). Swordsmen who walk the path of killing can store their Malice at Killing Sword Mountain by driving their sword into the rock, then draw on it to multiply the power of their attunement methods, though every warrior has a limit to how much Malice they can handle. Zane and Lily both learn to channel it through their blades.

name: Bryson Lowell
reason: The character's Chinese name Luo Bingquan was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Bryson' was chosen for the treacherous family patriarch, with the surname 'Lowell' binding him into Zane's family unit as his uncle.
description: Zane's uncle and the Lowell family patriarch who betrayed him (Eps 326-335). Terrified after discovering that the nephew he betrayed had survived and thrived in the Skyreach Sect, he desperately sought power and fell in with the fugitive Blood Prisoner, ignoring the disappearances it caused. Zane shatters his sword and he is executed in Ep 335, mirroring Luo Bingquan's execution in chapter 324 of the source.

name: Wheel of Reincarnation
reason: The source term 'Wheel of Reincarnation' (also rendered 'Wheel of Samsara' / 'Plate of Samsara') was carried over directly for the adaptation.
description: A massive spatial artifact claimed by Livingston and later brought under Zane's control (Eps 1164-1177). Fully activating it requires lighting all three thousand six hundred runes, after which Zane raises it from tens of thousands of miles beneath the earth and even rides it through battles, withstanding palm prints as large as the Wheel itself. He uses it to travel to the Endless Abyss.

name: Wheel
issues: Ambiguous short form referring to two different entities: in Eps 540-561 'the Wheel' is Vesper's Wheel of Fortune, while in Eps 1166-1177 it is the Wheel of Reincarnation. It cannot be aliased to a single canonical entity; its mentions should be apportioned by episode range.
reason: Bare 'Wheel' is a context-dependent short form of two separate canonical entities, kept only to flag the collision.
description: Shorthand used in the episodes for whichever wheel-artifact is on screen: Vesper's luck-testing Wheel of Fortune in the Eps 540-561 arc, and the colossal spatial Wheel of Reincarnation in the Eps 1164-1177 arc.

name: Wheel of Fortune
reason: The source term 'Wheel of Fortune' was carried over directly for the adaptation.
description: A luck-testing trial designed by Vesper and modeled on the Wheel of Fortune of the Upper World (Eps 540-885); it looks like a game but ejects rather than kills the cultivators who fail it. Vesper used it to find the luckiest warrior, with rich treasures as rewards: Tia was the third to complete it, and Zane won it, claiming the bone of a Cloud-Chaser Lion instead of an immortal's bone.

name: Fenton
reason: The character's Chinese name Sima Yulong was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Fenton', a crisp name befitting the sect's crown-jewel prodigy.
description: The greatest genius the Soulbound Sect has produced in generations and the crown jewel of its younger generation (Eps 1030-1045), in a class of his own among the talent at the Myriad Spirit House. Passed over by the Alliance in favor of Zane despite his far higher cultivation, he is pushed by the Saint Lord's faction into challenging Zane, and faces the jeering crowd without reacting. He corresponds to Sima Yulong, who duels Luo Zheng at the Dragon Tiger Palace in chapters 1007-1022.
